Chapter 04 of 19

Skytrain

Vancouver transit grid100 BPM
The story

Terminal City is spread out from the port to the park to the far side of the inlet, and all of it has to run on the same clock. That clock is the SkyTrain. Doors, chimes, arrivals, crossings, the same intervals repeating all day: a city-sized metronome that thousands of commuters happen to ride.

You will not see anything strange on the train itself. The evidence is in the timing. A train pulls in at the exact moment the Wire Choir changes its tune three districts away. Two things that have nothing to do with each other line up a little too perfectly. A door chime lands right on the beat of the song in your headphones.

The Old Line remembers routes the city forgot. The 3:17 Freight carries things away. The SkyTrain does neither. It only keeps time, and because it does, the rest of the city can agree on when things happen. On time. Between the lines. Every door opens at once.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
